lever: GABA availability: acute GAT-1 reuptake block (reversible) versus GABA-transaminase inactivation (irreversible, slow)
status: kept, conditional on O01/O04/O06 mapping to E2 (and E_GABA not above threshold)
action_required_and_context: Raise synaptic or ambient GABA in the slice at a concentration verified by a change in the recorded cells (sIPSC decay, tonic current); acute arm needs a reversible agent because the transaminase inactivator needs pre-incubation; context: Synapsin-Cre slice, layer II/III, P13-17, burst endpoint as LFP
compound_or_probe_sustained_by_a_documen: Probe classes only: a GAT-1 inhibitor with nanomolar uptake IC50 values and a transaminase inactivator with millimolar inactivation constants (IT46 reader, database/abstract depth; the inactivation constants of three documents are not comparable with each other). No compound is recommended
known_in_WWOX: WWOX: no measurement of GABA content, release or uptake; sIPSC amplitude -52%, frequency -18% in Synapsin-Cre slice (this package, measured); global-knockout hippocampal PV marker count -44% at 2 weeks (reused, partial full text, other model); vigabatrin exposure in WWOX children exists as case-level data in the repository (no instrument)
transferred_from_other_systems_named: E_GABA of WT cortex and hippocampus at P13-17 about -67 mV, n=5, pooled regions, other mouse models (Yuan 2019, IT46 reader, full text); GABA-raising drugs aggravate absence-type seizures (IT46 reader, cohorts); GAT-1 mRNA higher in astrocytes than in neurons in a P7 mouse table (transferred RNA)
risk_of_acting_on_a_compensation: if the sIPSC fall is a consequence of the bursting network (E5) or an adaptation, raising GABA targets the effect, not the cause; a bath reuptake blocker also acts on astrocytic uptake and raises tonic current, which is not synaptic inhibition
counter_evidence: seizure-type dependence (absence aggravation); GABA enrichment is not functional inhibition (DIS-017 revival trigger not fired); depolarising or shunting GABA at P13-17
result_that_would_reject_it: no reduction of bursts at a concentration that measurably raises tonic current or sIPSC decay in the same cells; or reduction equal to a non-GABAergic arm matched on measured cellular effect; or KO E_GABA at or above threshold
functional_comparator: a submaximal NMDAR block (d-APV) or a hyperpolarising manipulation matched on the recorded cells' membrane potential and input resistance; the endpoint is the burst LFP in the same slices [ADV-006 2026-11-14] The matching variable is stated differently in SCI42 new_measurements.tsv M10 (the same percent of evoked synaptic charge removed): CF23 in measurement_reconciliation_adv006_20261114/output/conflicts.tsv; not decided.
mechanism_comparator: gabazine or bicuculline reversal of the effect; sIPSC/tonic-current readout; GAT-1 selectivity check against astrocytic uptake
adds_over_general_anticonvulsant_action: Nothing beyond general anticonvulsant action unless E2 is shown (reduced GABA per event). A transaminase inactivator already used in children with WWOX-related epilepsy stays at its general rationale
depth_of_support: reader findings (abstract/database level) plus this package's source reading; not a WWOX datum; [V9] transfer sources behind this row (vigabatrin case data, P7 RNA table, PV marker count, Kv7/HCN notes, NKCC1 trials) were not re-opened by the verifier: UNVERIFIABLE by V9, reader depth only

lever: Postsynaptic GABA-A positive modulation (benzodiazepine-site class; a neurosteroid-type tonic-receptor modulator is a separate class)
status: kept, conditional on E3 (smaller mIPSC and smaller agonist response) in physiological chloride
action_required_and_context: Amplify existing GABA signalling at receptors; needs GABA release and a receptor population to act on; context: confirm the deficit with a physiological-chloride pipette, event identity by antagonist, mIPSC and agonist response in the same cells
compound_or_probe_sustained_by_a_documen: Class-level: benzodiazepine-site modulator (diazepam shifted the GABA EC50 from 41.0 to 21.7 uM in oocytes, reader, abstract); clobazam randomised trial in Lennox-Gastaut (placebo -12.1% against -68.3% drop seizures in the top-dose arm of three, abstract); ganaxolone (a neuroactive steroid acting on tonic receptors, not a benzodiazepine-site drug) against placebo in CDKL5 disorder (30.7% against 6.9% motor seizures, abstract). Not recommendations
known_in_WWOX: WWOX: benzodiazepines appear as co-therapy in the repository case table (two single-child reports of response, three groups with none, no instrument); no WWOX receptor datum
transferred_from_other_systems_named: oocytes and cultured cells (EC50 shift); animal febrile-seizure model where diazepam aggravated events at P11 but not P14 (Kasahara 2019, abstract); LGS and CDKL5 trials, not stratified by cause; OPC functional GABA-A in mouse cortex (abstract) so a bath modulator is not neuron-only [ADV-004 2026-11-14] Subtype wording that may be carried: in one laboratory's rat-subunit series N-desmethylclobazam potentiates alpha2 and alpha3 more than alpha1 in efficacy (printed ratio 1.77; beta isoform and Emax basis as stated in gabaa_subtype_adv004_20261114/README.md), a human-oocyte series points the same way on a total-response basis (1.33) and calls it non-selective, and no independent same-design replication with diazepam exists. Not carried: 'alpha2-preferring' as established, or a 'subtype-discriminating pair'.
risk_of_acting_on_a_compensation: if the amplitude fall is loss of inhibitory input (E1) a modulator amplifies a smaller remainder; if GABA is depolarising or excitatory (E4) a modulator may aggravate
counter_evidence: tolerance (14% lost response by year 3 in the LGS extension); depolarising GABA aggravation in immature animals; neurosteroid effect on tonic rather than synaptic receptors
result_that_would_reject_it: agonist response and mIPSC both normal (no receptor deficit); or burst reduction equal to a matched non-GABAergic arm; or KO E_GABA above threshold with aggravation
mechanism_comparator: antagonist occlusion; subunit-selective tool for the benzodiazepine site only if identity and action are sustained by a document (not done here)
adds_over_general_anticonvulsant_action: Only if a receptor or amplitude deficit is confirmed in physiological chloride; otherwise the rationale is the general anticonvulsant action of the class (benzodiazepine co-therapy is already recorded in WWOX children)
